newsitem.title: USA: U.S. King County bond issue heads for defeat.
newsitem.headline: U.S. King County bond issue heads for defeat.

text.p: A $216 million bond measure aimed at preserving and expanding Seattle's King County urban parklands was defeated by voters Tuesday.
With 99 percent of King County precincts reporting, 54 percent of voters favored the so-called "Field and Streams" measure, which required a supermajority of 60 percent to pass.
Up to a third of the county's votes were expected to be cast by absentee ballots, which had not yet been counted, but they were not expected to change the result.
A companion $30 million tax levy also appeared headed for defeat in King County, which includes Seattle and the surrounding area.
The 30-year bond issue would have provided new ball fields and open space projects and allowed for the preservation of stream and wildlife corridors.
Backers said they probably would bring the measures before voters again.
